prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1044; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a hit while turning left at an intersection and says the other vehicle came through on a green light as they were completing the turn. Reported injury is a concussion with headaches and dizziness, which is a plausible result for an impact of this kind.

Entry 2: Police report and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time and that the collision happened as described. Photos taken at the scene match the account given so far.

Entry 3: Claimant is not represented by a lawyer and handled the first call directly. Account given matches the initial report in every detail, including the order of events and the position of both vehicles.

Entry 4: Other driver confirms the collision occurred as described and does not dispute the sequence. Driver is named on the policy and the policy was in force at the time of loss.

Entry 5: Vehicle damage is mostly in line with the described impact to the driver side and front quarter panel. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or inspection records, and nothing suggests the damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 6: Medical records show the concussion was diagnosed and treated, and recovery has taken somewhat longer than usual for this injury. No earlier injury to the same area of the head or neck is known from prior records.

Entry 7: Claimant gave the same account in the follow-up call and again at the inspection. Nothing in the statements has changed on any point discussed so far.

Entry 8: File is progressing on the standard path with the medical treatment still ongoing. Next step is to request updated treatment notes and set a review once the claimant's provider issues a current prognosis.
